raw_case_text:
A 77-year-old man with unresectable malignant melanoma in the left nasal cavity was referred to our hospital. He had angina pectoris, hypertension, and lacunar infarction. He had no particular family history, and laboratory tests revealed no remarkable abnormality. He was administered nivolumab (3 mg/kg every 2 weeks) as first-line therapy. After the 4th infusion of nivolumab he developed polymyalgia rheumatica, which we considered an irAE. He was treated with prednisolone at a maintenance dose of 15 mg/day because exacerbation immediately occurred when tapering of prednisolone was attempted. After the 5th infusion of nivolumab, the nasal tumor increased in size, which was considered to be progressive disease.
Ipilimumab (3 mg/kg every 3 weeks) was administered as second-line therapy. After the 3rd infusion of ipilimumab he suffered from severe fatigue and paralytic ileus, which were attributed to ipilimumab, and was admitted to a local hospital. For this reason, ipilimumab therapy was discontinued; 4 weeks after the last infusion of ipilimumab, he developed grade 2 diarrhea that persisted for 10 days (Fig. 1).
Computed tomography revealed wall thickening of the sigmoid colon and rectum. Sigmoidoscopy confirmed signs of inflammation, with coarse mucosa that was easily bleeding and contained purulence and erosions; these endoscopic findings resembled ulcerative colitis (Fig. 2a). Infectious workup, including CMV antigenemia and Clostridium difficile in the stool, were negative. Based on these findings, he was diagnosed with irColitis. Two weeks after the onset of diarrhea he was transferred to our hospital and was treated with daily intravenous 45 mg of methylprednisolone (1 mg/kg), which led to a rapid reduction in the frequency of diarrhea.
On the 6th day after hospitalization, sigmoidoscopy showed mucosal healing in the rectum (Fig. 2b). On the 7th day after hospitalization, methylprednisolone was reduced to 35 mg/day, but hematochezia and anemia were observed the following day. To confirm the source of bleeding, left-sided colonoscopy was performed on the 12th day after hospitalization and revealed multiple punched-out ulcers in the descending colon, but the remission in the sigmoid colon and rectum was maintained (Fig. 2c). Histologic examination of the biopsy samples from the ulcers showed crypt abscesses and infiltration of lymphocytes and plasma cells (Fig. 2d). Immunohistochemical study was positive for CMV (Fig. 2e), although CMV pp65 antigenemia was negative. He was diagnosed with CMV colitis, for which ganciclovir (5 mg/kg) twice daily was initiated. Methylprednisolone was tapered to 30 mg/day.
On the 27th day after hospitalization, total colonoscopy showed ulcers with healing tendency in the ascending and descending colon. However, the hematochezia and anemia did not improve. To rule out bleeding from the small intestine, video capsule endoscopy was performed on the 33rd day after hospitalization and revealed active bleeding from the ileum. On the 36th day after hospitalization, double balloon enteroscopy showed ulcers with healing tendency in the ileum (Fig. 2f). Although CMV was not detected from the biopsy samples of ileal ulcers at this time, this healing tendency could be due to the antiviral therapy. Thereafter, there was no recurrence of the hematochezia, and the anemia improved gradually. On the 40th day after hospitalization, ganciclovir was discontinued and steroids were tapered gradually. He was discharged on the 69th day after hospitalization.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 77-year-old man with unresectable nasal malignant melanoma presented with persistent grade 2 diarrhea 4 weeks after his third infusion of ipilimumab, followed on hospital day 8 by acute hematochezia and anemia.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Treated first-line with nivolumab (5 infusions; complicated after dose 4 by steroid-dependent polymyalgia rheumatica maintained on prednisolone 15 mg/day) and second-line with ipilimumab (3 infusions of 3 mg/kg q3w, discontinued after dose 3 due to severe fatigue and paralytic ileus), the patient developed persistent grade 2 diarrhea 4 weeks after his last ipilimumab dose. Transferred to our hospital 2 weeks into the diarrheal illness and treated with IV methylprednisolone (45 mg/day, 1 mg/kg) for immune-related colitis with rapid improvement in diarrhea and rectal healing by day 6, he developed acute hematochezia and anemia on hospital day 8, one day after tapering methylprednisolone to 35 mg/day.
subjective.past_medical_history: Unresectable left nasal cavity malignant melanoma status post nivolumab and ipilimumab immunotherapy; nivolumab-induced polymyalgia rheumatica; angina pectoris, hypertension, and lacunar cerebral infarction.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for persistent diarrhea, prior ipilimumab-related severe fatigue and paralytic ileus, and hospital day 8 hematochezia. Medications: prednisolone 15 mg/day escalated to IV methylprednisolone 45 mg/day.

objective.routine_investigations: Baseline infectious workup at onset of diarrhea—including peripheral blood CMV pp65 antigenemia and stool Clostridioides difficile testing—was negative. On hospital day 8, anemia developed alongside persistent hematochezia; repeat CMV pp65 antigenemia on day 12 remained negative.
objective.advanced_workup: Initial abdominal CT showed wall thickening of the sigmoid colon and rectum, and initial sigmoidoscopy showed friable, easily bleeding, purulent, eroded rectosigmoid mucosa resembling ulcerative colitis (mucosal healing of the rectum seen on day 6 sigmoidoscopy). Following hematochezia on day 8, left-sided colonoscopy on hospital day 12 revealed maintained rectosigmoid remission but multiple new punched-out ulcers in the descending colon; biopsy histology demonstrated crypt abscesses, lymphoplasmacytic infiltration, and positive cytomegalovirus (CMV) immunohistochemistry despite negative blood CMV pp65 antigenemia. Day 27 total colonoscopy showed healing ascending and descending colon ulcers, while day 33 video capsule endoscopy and day 36 double-balloon enteroscopy identified active bleeding from healing ileal ulcers (ileal biopsy CMV-negative during ganciclovir therapy).

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Diagnosed with ipilimumab-induced immune-related colitis (irColitis) complicated during corticosteroid treatment by cytomegalovirus (CMV) enterocolitis presenting with descending colon and ileal punched-out ulcers and lower GI hemorrhage, confirmed by positive CMV immunohistochemistry on descending colon ulcer biopsy despite negative peripheral blood CMV pp65 antigenemia. Treated with intravenous ganciclovir (5 mg/kg twice daily from hospital day 12 to day 40) while gradually tapering methylprednisolone (to 30 mg/day and then off), resulting in healing of colonic and ileal ulcers on colonoscopy and double-balloon enteroscopy, resolution of hematochezia and anemia, and hospital discharge on day 69.
